title: toolcall-envelope-segment-offset-on-vpc-proxy-failover
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers on Private (VPC) reported tool/function-call responses where structured JSON payloads were mis-parsed and function outputs were misattributed after an upstream proxy failover. Failure mode: envelope segment offsets are shifted by a small byte delta during proxy reconnection/replay which leads to the runtime reassembly logic appending overlapped bytes and corrupting the length-prefixed JSON envelope. This causes downstream structured-output parsers to either throw parse errors or attach fields to the wrong tool invocation when the runtime remaps session tags.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use a VPC-private runtime with proxy configured (customer-simulated env)
2) Send a streaming invocation invoking a tool (function call) that emits multiple JSON envelopes separated by our envelope delimiter and length header
3) During mid-stream emission, simulate proxy failover: drop TCP then restore (iptables DROP/ACCEPT) to force reconnect and buffered replay from proxy
4) Observe the runtime logs for 'envelope-reassembly-offset-mismatch' and compare parsed JSON segments to raw bytes; repro verified locally with proxy-replay waveform script
5) Customer repro scripts attached in attachments folder (CASE-8712 repro.sh)
observed_behavior: Structured JSON tool outputs intermittently fail to parse (JSONDecodeError) or parse with shifted fields
Function call responses are occasionally attributed to upstream invocation IDs that are off by one or have stale session tags
Errors spike during proxy reconnect windows and after load-balancer failovers in the customer VPC (observed within 10-30s windows)
Affected only on Private (VPC) and Private+Dedicated hybrid customers using our proxy replay feature; Hosted customers not impacted in observed incidents
impact_summary: High severity customer-facing data corruption: customer applications receiving malformed/incorrect tool outputs, multiple P1/P0 escalations from three enterprise customers, potential data leakage risk if outputs get misattributed across tenants (no confirmed cross-tenant leakage yet). Immediate mitigation required to stop production parse failures and restore trust.
customer_reports: CASE-8712: Large fintech tenant - intermittent JSON parse failures, production impact on payouts pipeline
CASE-8799: HealthCareCo - structured output fields missing or duplicated after gateway failover
CASE-8808: RetailCorp - canary tests showed 1.8% of invocations had misattributed tool outputs during peak deploys
hypothesis_root_causes: Proxy replay logic concatenates buffered tail segments without preserving original segment byte offsets or explicit segment sequence IDs
Runtime reassembly assumes monotonic segment framing and uses byte-length heuristics, which fail when overlapping replayed bytes are present
Session tag rebind occurs on reconnect and runtime tries to map buffered fragments to the 'latest' session, causing off-by-one envelope mappings
temporary_mitigations: Disable proxy-side buffered replay for affected customers (config change) - reduces occurrence to zero but increases request latency on reconnect
Apply a conservative parser fallback: if envelope header checksum mismatch -> drop fragment and request client retry (adds latency but prevents corrupt application-level outputs)
Customer guidance: schedule maintenance windows for load-balancer changes until patch is deployed
proposed_fix: Patch proxy replay layer to attach explicit 64-bit segment sequence IDs and original byte offset metadata to each buffered chunk
Update runtime reassembly to validate sequence IDs and to deduplicate overlapped byte ranges based on offset metadata (prefer explicit offset over heuristics)
Add an envelope header CRC and session-tag binding check; if mismatch, reject replayed fragments and surface a structured error to the control plane
Backfill: run a one-off sanitization pass to detect misattributed responses in affected tenants using historical logs and optionally replay corrected envelopes (opt-in with customer approval)
testing_plan: Unit tests for reassembly code that simulate overlapped buffers and verify deterministic dedupe behavior
Integration test harness that simulates proxy failover and buffered replay (scriptable via CI)
Fuzz tests for envelope header parsing, length fields, CRC mismatch handling
Canary deploy against internal 'canary-tenant-1' and one low-traffic paying customer with explicit opt-in
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime and proxy fixes to runtime-hotfix branch and run full integration suite
2) Deploy to internal staging and run 48h soak with simulated replay scenarios
3) Canary rollout to canary-tenant-1 (2% traffic) for 24h, monitor parse-error rate and customer-facing metrics
4) Gradual rollout to affected customers with coordinated maintenance windows and post-deploy validation scripts
5) Full rollout to all Private/Dedicated within 7 days if canary passes
monitoring_queries: sum(parse_errors) by route where env = 'private' and error_type = 'JSONDecodeError' over 1m
count(toolcall_misattribution_events) by tenant over 1h where timestamp >= '2026-03-09'
notes: Eng lead: prioritize runtime reassembly change as P0; expected cross-team work with proxy and infra
PM notified (Jin Park) and CS engaged for coordinated customer communication
Design decision trade-offs: adding sequence IDs increases envelope header size by 8 bytes; acceptable for Private customers but evaluate cost for Hosted paths
Postmortem required after full mitigation; include timeline and customer impact numbers
